**PREAMBLE**

The Murray Basin Rail Maintenance Committee (hereafter "the Committee") is established as a standing advisory and coordination body to assist the Department of Transport and Planning (DTP) in the planning, prioritisation, and oversight of maintenance activities across the Murray Basin rail network. The Committee operates within the framework of the Victorian Rail Infrastructure Maintenance Policy and reports directly to the Deputy Secretary, Rail Infrastructure Division.

The Committee is established under the authority of the Secretary, Department of Transport and Planning, pursuant to the Transport Integration Act 2010 (Vic) and the Rail Management Act 1996 (Vic).

Murray Basin Rail Maintenance Committee established 2018-03-14 date. Record status: current.

---

**SECTION 1: PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES**

1.1 The principal purpose of the Committee is to provide coordinated, evidence-based advice to DTP on the prioritisation of maintenance works, condition monitoring, and capital renewal programs across the Murray Basin rail network.

1.2 The specific objectives of the Committee are:

(a) To review and recommend annual maintenance work programs for the network segments comprising the Murray Basin corridor, including but not limited to the Mildura, Robinvale, Manangatang, and Sea Lake lines;

(b) To monitor the condition of track, structures, signalling, and level crossings, and to advise on emerging risks requiring intervention;

(c) To facilitate communication and information sharing among rail infrastructure managers, passenger and freight operators, local government authorities, and other stakeholders operating within the Murray Basin region;

(d) To review and endorse maintenance standards, inspection frequencies, and engineering practices proposed for application on the network;

(e) To identify opportunities for efficiency improvements, including the coordination of track closures, possession scheduling, and the sharing of plant and equipment;

(f) To report to DTP on the performance of maintenance activities, including expenditure against approved budgets, delivery against program milestones, and the results of post-works inspections;

(g) To undertake such other functions as DTP may from time to time direct in writing.

---

**SECTION 2: MEMBERSHIP AND APPOINTMENT**

2.1 The Committee shall comprise no fewer than nine (9) and no more than thirteen (13) voting members, appointed by the Deputy Secretary, Rail Infrastructure Division, for a term of two (2) years, renewable at the discretion of DTP.

2.2 Membership categories shall be as follows:

(a) **Chairperson** — appointed by DTP from among senior officers of the Rail Infrastructure Division;

(b) **DTP Representatives** — two officers nominated by the Deputy Secretary, Rail Infrastructure Division;

(c) **Infrastructure Manager Representatives** — three officers nominated by the relevant rail infrastructure manager(s) for the Murray Basin network;

(d) **Operator Representatives** — two officers nominated jointly by the passenger and freight operators using the Murray Basin corridor;

(e) **Local Government Representatives** — one officer nominated by the Murray Basin Rail Liaison Group, representing the interests of the municipalities traversed by the network;

**1. Purpose**

1.1 This Amendment amends the Murray Basin Rail Maintenance Committee Charter (“the Charter”) adopted on 14 March 2018, as previously amended by Amendment No. 1 (effective 1 September 2019) and Amendment No. 2 (effective 15 January 2021).

1.2 The amendment adjusts the quorum requirements for decision-making by the Committee and introduces a contingency provision for remote participation. The changes respond to the Committee’s experience during the 2020–21 maintenance planning cycle, during which three scheduled meetings were unable to proceed because the required quorum could not be achieved, and to the increased reliance on teleconference and video-conference participation since March 2020.

**2. Amendments to Clause 8 (Quorum and Decision-Making)**

2.1 Clause 8.1 of the Charter is deleted and replaced with the following:

> 8.1 A quorum shall consist of not fewer than five (5) voting members, of whom at least one (1) shall be a representative of the Department of Transport (DTP) and at least one (1) shall be a representative of a rail infrastructure manager (V/Line or ARTC). A member participating by telephone or video-conference shall be counted toward the quorum, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants and has confirmed their attendance in accordance with Clause 8.4.

2.2 Clause 8.2 of the Charter is deleted and replaced with the following:

> 8.2 Where, thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed for a meeting, a quorum is not present, the Chair shall adjourn the meeting. The Chair may reconvene the meeting at a later time on the same day, or on a date not more than fourteen (14) days thereafter. If a quorum is still not present at the reconvened meeting, the Chair may, with the written consent of the Deputy Secretary, DTP Regional Rail Delivery, proceed with the meeting on the basis of a reduced quorum of not fewer than three (3) voting members, provided that:
>
> (a) the reduced quorum includes at least one (1) DTP representative and at least one (1) rail infrastructure manager representative;
>
> (b) any decision made at such a meeting is recorded as provisional and is subject to ratification at the next meeting at which a full quorum is present; and
>
> (c) the Chair reports the circumstances of the reduced-quorum meeting to the Deputy Secretary within five (5) business days.

2.3 Clause 8.3 of the Charter is amended by deleting the words “a simple majority of those present and voting” and substituting “a simple majority of those present and voting, provided that a quorum exists at the time the vote is taken”.

2.4 A new Clause 8.5 is inserted after Clause 8.4, as follows:

> 8.5 For the purposes of this Clause, a “voting member” is a member appointed under Clause 4 whose appointment is current and who has not been excused from voting under Clause 9.3. Alternate members attending in place of an appointed member shall have the same voting rights as the member they replace, but no member may hold more than one vote.

**3. Rationale**

3.1 The previous quorum requirement of six (6) voting members, including at least two (2) representatives of rail infrastructure managers, proved difficult to satisfy during the 2020–21 period. Of the twelve (12) meetings scheduled between April 2020 and April 2021, three (3) were cancelled due to lack of quorum, and two (2) others proceeded only after the agenda was reduced to items not requiring a formal vote.

**6. ANNUAL REVIEW AND PERFORMANCE REPORTING**

6.1 The Committee shall conduct a formal review of its performance and operations at least once in each calendar year. The review shall be tabled at the first ordinary meeting of the Committee held after the anniversary of the Charter’s adoption, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

6.2 The purpose of the annual review is to assess the effectiveness of the Committee in fulfilling its functions under Clause 3, to identify any impediments to the timely delivery of maintenance works across the Murray Basin rail network, and to recommend improvements to the Charter, the Committee’s operating procedures, or the coordination arrangements with infrastructure managers and freight operators.

6.3 The annual review shall consider, at a minimum:

- progress against the Committee’s annual work plan;
- the timeliness and quality of advice provided to the Secretary of the Department of Transport and Planning (DTP);
- the effectiveness of consultation arrangements with stakeholders, including freight operators, local councils, and grain producers;
- the adequacy of resourcing and secretariat support;
- the accuracy and currency of the Committee’s records, including the membership register and the register of declared interests;
- any matters referred to the Committee by the Minister, the Secretary, or the Rail Infrastructure Manager – ARTC.

6.4 The Chair shall prepare a written report of the annual review, to be submitted to the Secretary of DTP within 30 days of the meeting at which the review is considered. The report shall include:

- a summary of the Committee’s activities during the period under review;
- a statement of achievements against the objectives set out in Clause 3;
- a description of any challenges or difficulties encountered, including any delays in the delivery of maintenance works and the reasons for those delays;
- recommendations for the coming year, including any proposed amendments to the Charter;
- a record of the attendance of members at Committee meetings during the period under review.

6.5 The annual review for the period 1 March 2022 to 28 February 2023 was tabled at the Committee meeting of 30 March 2023. The review noted the following achievements:

- completion of the gauge widening risk assessment on the Mildura Line, as recommended in the 2021 review;
- establishment of a joint working group with ARTC and V/Line to coordinate planned maintenance closures with grain harvest logistics;
- adoption of a revised communication protocol for track closure notifications to freight operators, reducing the average notice period from 14 days to 10 days.

6.6 The review also identified the following challenges:

- ongoing difficulty in securing track access windows during peak harvest periods, particularly on the Ouyen–Murrayville section;
- a shortage of qualified track maintenance personnel in the Mildura region, leading to the deferral of some routine inspections;
- inconsistencies in the reporting of rail corrugation factor (RCF) data between ARTC and V/Line, which have impeded the prioritisation of grinding works.

6.7 The Committee recommends that, in the coming year, DTP give priority to:

- funding a targeted recruitment and training program for track maintenance staff in the north-west region;

Kowalski presented the findings of the ultrasonic rail inspection and track geometry survey conducted on 8 and 9 July 2019 on Section 14 of the Mildura Line. The inspection was undertaken as part of the pre-closure assessment ahead of the planned maintenance possession scheduled for late August.

Key findings were tabled:

- **Rail Corrugation Factor (RCF):** Moderate corrugation observed on the high rail of the curve at approximately KM 291.2. The RCF reading was 0.42, which is below the intervention threshold of 0.50 but above the monitoring level of 0.35. Kowalski recommended that this section be included in the grinding program for the August possession.
- **Gauge Widening Risk (GWR):** A GWR assessment identified a section of approximately 80 metres at KM 295.8 where gauge widening was noted. The reading was 8 mm, which is within the acceptable tolerance but trending upward. A temporary speed restriction of 60 km/h was implemented on 10 July 2019 as a precautionary measure. This restriction will remain in place until the resleepering works are completed in the August possession.
- **Rail Defects:** Two internal rail defects (one at KM 289.4, one at KM 298.1) were identified during the ultrasonic inspection. Both defects were classified as Class 2 (non-urgent) and have been scheduled for repair during the August possession. Replacement rail segments (12 m and 9 m respectively) have been ordered and are expected to arrive at the Ouyen depot by 5 August 2019.
- **Ballast Condition:** The ballast shoulder on the northern side of the track between KM 299.0 and KM 300.2 was found to be deficient, with a reduced shoulder width of approximately 150 mm. This section will be included in the regrading program.

Nair queried whether the temporary speed restriction had been communicated to all relevant parties, including freight operators. Kowalski confirmed that the restriction had been issued via the daily network notice on 10 July 2019 and that all affected operators had been advised by email. Nair requested that the restriction also be noted in the weekly safety bulletin for the week commencing 22 July 2019.

Brooks asked whether the cost of the additional rail defect repairs had been accounted for in the current maintenance budget. Kowalski advised that the cost of the two replacement rail segments (approximately $18,000 including delivery) would be absorbed within the existing track maintenance allocation for the 2019/20 financial year. The chair called the meeting to order at 10:05 AM and welcomed Ms. Nguyen, who had been invited to provide an overview of the department’s funding position for the coming financial year.

Brooks tabled the final financial report for the 2018/19 financial year. The committee noted that the final expenditure for the year was $4,182,300, representing a variance of –$17,700 (0.4%) against the approved allocation of $4,200,000. **9.2 Allocation for 2019/20 – Regional Rail Renewals Program**

Nguyen provided a summary of the department’s funding decision for the 2019/20 financial year. She advised that the committee’s request for an additional $350,000 for the Regional Rail Renewals Program had been considered, but that the department had approved a total allocation of $4,150,000 for the committee’s maintenance activities for the year. This represented an increase of $150,000 over the 2018/19 base allocation, but was $200,000 less than the amount requested.

Nguyen explained that the department had prioritised funding for the resleepering of the Ouyen–Murrayville line, which had been identified as a critical constraint for grain freight movements during the harvest period. She noted that the department expected the committee to manage the program within the approved allocation and that any additional expenditure would require a formal variation request.

2.8 The Chairperson shall:

(c) represent the Committee to DTP and other external stakeholders as required;

(d) monitor the implementation of the Committee’s decisions and recommendations; and

(e) perform such other duties as DTP may direct from time to time.

**SECTION 3: MEETINGS AND QUORUM**

3.1 The Committee shall meet no fewer than four (4) times per calendar year. The Chairperson may convene additional meetings as required.

3.2 A quorum shall consist of not less than half of the appointed voting members, plus the Chairperson or the Chairperson’s nominated deputy. No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present.

3.3 Meetings shall be held in person, by video conference, or by a combination of both, as determined by the Chairperson. In-person meetings shall ordinarily be held at a venue within the Murray Basin region, with the location rotated among member organisations where practicable.

3.4 Notice of each meeting shall be given at least fourteen (14) days in advance, accompanied by the agenda and relevant papers. Urgent matters may be considered at shorter notice with the agreement of a simple majority of voting members.

3.5 Decisions of the Committee shall be made by a simple majority of voting members present and voting. The Chairperson shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a casting vote.

**2. Amendments to Clause 8 (Quorum and Decision-Making)**

2.1 Clause 8.1 of the Charter is deleted and replaced with the following:

> 8.1 A quorum shall consist of not fewer than five (5) voting members, of whom at least one (1) shall be a representative of the Department of Transport (DTP) and at least one (1) shall be a representative of a rail infrastructure manager (V/Line or ARTC). A member participating by telephone or video-conference shall be counted toward the quorum, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants and has confirmed their attendance in accordance with Clause 8.4.

2.2 Clause 8.2 of the Charter is deleted and replaced with the following:

> 8.2 Where, thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed for a meeting, a quorum is not present, the Chair shall adjourn the meeting. The Chair may reconvene the meeting at a later time on the same day, or on a date not more than fourteen (14) days thereafter. If a quorum is still not present at the reconvened meeting, the Chair may, with the written consent of the Deputy Secretary, DTP Regional Rail Delivery, proceed with the meeting on the basis of a reduced quorum of not fewer than three (3) voting members, provided that:
>
> (a) the reduced quorum includes at least one (1) DTP representative and at least one (1) rail infrastructure manager representative;
>
> (b) any decision made at such a meeting is recorded as provisional and is subject to ratification at the next meeting at which a full quorum is present; and
>
> (c) the Chair reports the circumstances of the reduced-quorum meeting to the Deputy Secretary within five (5) business days.

2.3 Clause 8.3 of the Charter is amended by deleting the words “a simple majority of those present and voting” and substituting “a simple majority of those present and voting, provided that a quorum exists at the time the vote is taken”.

2.4 A new Clause 8.5 is inserted after Clause 8.4, as follows:

> 8.5 For the purposes of this Clause, a “voting member” is a member appointed under Clause 4 whose appointment is current and who has not been excused from voting under Clause 9.3. Alternate members attending in place of an appointed member shall have the same voting rights as the member they replace, but no member may hold more than one vote.

**3. Rationale**

3.1 The previous quorum requirement of six (6) voting members, including at least two (2) representatives of rail infrastructure managers, proved difficult to satisfy during the 2020–21 period. Of the twelve (12) meetings scheduled between April 2020 and April 2021, three (3) were cancelled due to lack of quorum, and two (2) others proceeded only after the agenda was reduced to items not requiring a formal vote.

**ITEM 7 – OUYEN JUNCTION MAJOR RENEWAL – PLANNING UPDATE**

Chen presented a status update on the planning for the major renewal of Ouyen Junction. The renewal had been identified as a priority in the 2018 track condition assessment and was currently in the detailed design phase.

Chen reported that the design work was approximately 70% complete. The scope of the renewal included:
- Replacement of the turnout timbers on the main line and the two crossover roads.
- Regrading of the ballast profile across the junction.
- Replacement of the rail on the loop road (approx. 400 m).
- Installation of new gauge rods and switch lubricators.

The committee discussed the scheduling of the renewal. Chen noted that the preferred timing was during a dedicated possession in late 2021, to avoid conflict with the annual harvest period. He advised that a preliminary date of 18 October 2021 had been proposed for the commencement of the possession. This date had been selected to align with a lull in freight movements and to allow sufficient time for the works to be completed before the summer heat restrictions.

Okafor queried whether the renewal had been coordinated with the planned sleeper replacement on the Ouyen–Murrayville Line. Chen confirmed that the two programs were being managed separately but that the junction renewal would not overlap with the sleeper replacement works in 2019. The sleeper replacement scheduled for the August window was a separate, interim measure.

The chair requested that a formal project plan, including a risk assessment and a resource plan, be tabled at the September meeting.

**ITEM 8 – INSPECTION FINDINGS – MILDURA LINE, SECTION 14 (KM 287.5 – KM 302.0)**

Kowalski presented the findings of the ultrasonic rail inspection and track geometry survey conducted on 8 and 9 July 2019 on Section 14 of the Mildura Line. The inspection was undertaken as part of the pre-closure assessment ahead of the planned maintenance possession scheduled for late August.

Key findings were tabled:

- **Rail Corrugation Factor (RCF):** Moderate corrugation observed on the high rail of the curve at approximately KM 291.2. The RCF reading was 0.42, which is below the intervention threshold of 0.50 but above the monitoring level of 0.35. Kowalski recommended that this section be included in the grinding program for the August possession.
- **Gauge Widening Risk (GWR):** A GWR assessment identified a section of approximately 80 metres at KM 295.8 where gauge widening was noted. The reading was 8 mm, which is within the acceptable tolerance but trending upward. A temporary speed restriction of 60 km/h was implemented on 10 July 2019 as a precautionary measure. This restriction will remain in place until the resleepering works are completed in the August possession.
- **Rail Defects:** Two internal rail defects (one at KM 289.4, one at KM 298.1) were identified during the ultrasonic inspection. Both defects were classified as Class 2 (non-urgent) and have been scheduled for repair during the August possession. Replacement rail segments (12 m and 9 m respectively) have been ordered and are expected to arrive at the Ouyen depot by 5 August 2019.
- **Ballast Condition:** The ballast shoulder on the northern side of the track between KM 299.0 and KM 300.2 was found to be deficient, with a reduced shoulder width of approximately 150 mm. This section will be included in the regrading program.

Nair queried whether the temporary speed restriction had been communicated to all relevant parties, including freight operators. Kowalski confirmed that the restriction had been issued via the daily network notice on 10 July 2019 and that all affected operators had been advised by email. Nair requested that the restriction also be noted in the weekly safety bulletin for the week commencing 22 July 2019.

Brooks asked whether the cost of the additional rail defect repairs had been accounted for in the current maintenance budget. Kowalski advised that the cost of the two replacement rail segments (approximately $18,000 including delivery) would be absorbed within the existing track maintenance allocation for the 2019/20 financial year. Brooks noted that this would result in a variance of approximately $4,500 against the original allocation for rail replacement materials, and requested that the variance be formally recorded in the next financial report.

**Decision 8.1:** The committee accepted the inspection findings as tabled and agreed that the identified defects and deficiencies be addressed during the August 2019 possession.

**ITEM 9 – ANNUAL BUDGET REVIEW 2019/20**

The chair called the meeting to order at 10:05 AM and welcomed Ms. Nguyen, who had been invited to provide an overview of the department’s funding position for the coming financial year.

**9.1 Financial Report – 2018/19 Final Position**

Brooks tabled the final financial report for the 2018/19 financial year. The committee noted that the final expenditure for the year was $4,182,300, representing a variance of –$17,700 (0.4%) against the approved allocation of $4,200,000. The variance was primarily attributable to favourable pricing on ballast supply contracts and a reduction in the number of emergency call-outs during the autumn period.

The chair noted that the 2018/19 report would be forwarded to the department as part of the annual acquittal process. Brooks confirmed that the report had been prepared in accordance with the standard reporting framework and that all supporting documentation, including purchase orders and invoices, had been filed in the corporate records system.

**9.2 Allocation for 2019/20 – Regional Rail Renewals Program**

Nguyen provided a summary of the department’s funding decision for the 2019/20 financial year. She advised that the committee’s request for an additional $350,000 for the Regional Rail Renewals Program had been considered, but that the department had approved a total allocation of $4,150,000 for the committee’s maintenance activities for the year. This represented an increase of $150,000 over the 2018/19 base allocation, but was $200,000 less than the amount requested.

Nguyen explained that the department had prioritised funding for the resleepering of the Ouyen–Murrayville line, which had been identified as a critical constraint for grain freight movements during the harvest period. She noted that the department expected the committee to manage the program within the approved allocation and that any additional expenditure would require a formal variation request.

Brooks asked whether the department had provided any guidance on the expected timing of the funding transfer. Nguyen advised that the first quarterly instalment of $1,037,500 would be transferred to the committee’s account on 15 August 2019, with subsequent instalments to follow on 15 November 2019, 15 February 2020, and 15 May 2020.

Kowalski noted that the reduced allocation would require a review of the proposed resleepering program for the year. He advised that the program had been developed on the basis of the requested $4.5 million and that the committee would need to identify which sections of track could be deferred to a later year. Nair asked whether the department had indicated any flexibility in the allocation, and Nguyen advised that the approved amount was final.

**Decision 9.1:** The committee accepted the department’s funding decision for 2019/20 and agreed that the track maintenance program be revised to align with the approved allocation of $4,150,000. Kowalski was requested to provide a revised program at the next meeting.
